title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
authors: Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder, Melanie Subbiah, Jared Kaplan, Prafulla Dhariwal, Arvind Neelakantan, Pranav Shyam, Girish Sastry, Amanda Askell, Sandhini Agarwal, Ariel Herbert-Voss, Gretchen Krueger, Tom Henighan, Rewon Child, Aditya Ramesh, Daniel M. Ziegler, Jeffrey Wu, Clemens Winter, Christopher Hesse, Mark Chen, Eric Sigler, Mateusz Litwin, Scott Gray, Benjamin Chess, Jack Clark, Christopher Berner, Sam McCandlish, Alec Radford, Ilya Sutskever, Dario Amodei (31 authors)

code.title: openai/gpt-3
code.note: no code and no weights (API only): the repository holds the synthetic arithmetic and word-scramble sets, 500 uncurated 175B samples, per-language statistics of the training mix, examples of 13-gram overlaps and the model card

paper_note: 75 pages (40 + 32 of appendices); very long, read §1, §2, §3.9, §4 and §5 first
takeaway: Scaling a plain GPT decoder to 175B params (300B tokens, ~3640 pfs-days) makes in-context learning emerge: tasks specified by prompt alone, no fine-tuning, often near fine-tuned SOTA.
verdict: Believe the trend: across 41 accuracy tasks and eight sizes, larger models gain more from examples in the prompt. Treat any single score as one prompt and one draw of examples, with no error bars, mostly on development sets, partly contaminated, and compared with fine-tuned systems that ran under different rules.

headline.k: few-shot minus zero-shot, averaged over 41 accuracy tasks, from 125M to 175B
headline.d: recomputed from Table H.1: larger models use the prompt better

headline.k: few-shot, closed book, no gradient updates

resources.t: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
resources.n: the paper's missing error bar: on GPT-3 2.7B, the order of the same four examples moves SST-2 accuracy from 54.3% to 93.4%.

resources.t: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
resources.n: evidence on the paper's open question: random labels in the examples barely hurt, so the examples mostly teach format and label space.
a candidate mechanism for in-context learning, from several of GPT-3's authors.

resources.t: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
resources.n: re-scores the GPT-3 family's arithmetic with continuous metrics and argues the sharp jumps come from exact-match scoring.

kb.n: 2017: GPT-3 is the decoder half of the Transformer scaled about three orders of magnitude.

kb.t: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
kb.n: January 2020, the direct motivation (Kaplan and McCandlish are authors of both): GPT-3 extends the loss power law two more orders of magnitude and sized its models by it.
2022: 175B parameters on 300B tokens is heavily undertrained; rebalanced the parameters-to-tokens ratio GPT-3 popularised.
2018: the rival paradigm (bidirectional, fine-tuned) this paper displaced; the authors blame part of GPT-3's comparison-task failures on lacking bidirectionality.
2019: seven months earlier and pointing the other way, fine-tuning an encoder-decoder; T5-11B is the closed-book QA and compute baseline here.
2022: RLHF on GPT-3 to fix the instruction-following and alignment gaps documented here.
2019: tensor parallelism within each matrix multiply, one of the two model-parallel axes GPT-3 used.
2019: the memory optimisations that make 100B-plus dense training feasible.
